Sepsis after a sore throat

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A previously healthy 19-year-old has recurrent high fever one week after a sore throat seemed to improve. He now has unilateral neck tenderness and pleuritic pain. CT shows internal jugular thrombosis and multiple peripheral cavitating lung nodules. Which syndrome is most likely?

  1. Lemierre syndrome
  2. Right-sided infective endocarditis
  3. Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
  4. Primary pulmonary tuberculosis
  5. Bland venous thromboembolism
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Lemierre syndrome

Postpharyngeal sepsis with internal jugular septic thrombophlebitis and pulmonary septic emboli is characteristic of Lemierre syndrome.

Understanding the options

Lemierre syndrome
Postpharyngeal sepsis with internal jugular septic thrombophlebitis and pulmonary septic emboli is characteristic of Lemierre syndrome.
Right-sided infective endocarditis
This may cause septic pulmonary emboli, but the postpharyngitis internal jugular thrombosis localizes the primary septic source to the neck.
Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
Cavitating lung nodules can occur, but septic jugular thrombosis after pharyngitis favors Lemierre syndrome.
Primary pulmonary tuberculosis
Tuberculosis does not explain this acute postpharyngitis septic thrombophlebitis pattern.
Bland venous thromboembolism
Bland emboli do not explain high fever and multiple septic-appearing cavitating nodules after a neck infection.
